Thanks for the draft DPA annex — our legal team has a few follow-ups focused on technical safeguards and proof points to close our internal DPF review. Can you confirm or provide: 

- Concrete evidence of encryption in transit and at rest (algorithms, KMS provider, key rotation cadence).

We typically accept a short evidence pack (spreadsheet mapping controls to evidence artifacts + a single diagram/PDF). Is that something you can share by EOD Tuesday?

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helixtx.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-border technical evidence for DPA annex

Hi Oliver — thanks, and absolutely. I've pulled together an initial evidence pack and a plain-English mapping for your legal team. Highlights below; full items attached. Happy to walk through live if that helps.

Quick answers: 
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest. Keys stored in customer-segregated KMS namespaces (AWS KMS for hosted customers, customer-managed keys available for Dedicated/Private). Rotation: 90 days for service keys, customer keys follow customer policy.
- Subprocessors: Current roster included in the spreadsheet; each entry lists DPA status and SCC adoption where applicable.
- Processing regions: Primary inference occurs in EU regions for EU-tagged workloads (we pin inference to customer-chosen region). The topology PDF shows fallback paths and where KV cache replicas may exist — we call out TTLs.
- Supplementary measures: Customer-key separation, per-tenant key encryption, limited mem-caching of input data, strict egress filtering, and contractual prohibitions on onward transfers without customer consent.
- Logs & audits: Retention: 90 days by default for request traces; extended retention options available under Dedicated/Private. We included sample audit log snippets with redacted identifiers.

Attached: 
- redwood-dpf-evidence-mapping.xlsx (control-to-evidence map)
- network-topology-plain.pdf (processing/region fallback diagram)
- sccs-signed-template.pdf (template SCCs we rely on; execution copy on request)

I'll loop in our privacy SME and legal reviewer internally to confirm any outstanding items. If you want a single point-by-point doc in the worksheet format you sent, we can populate that as well.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Hi Oliver — following up with the consolidated evidence pack and short clarifications from our SMEs (see inline). We attached the populated worksheet and a sanitized audit log snippet per your ask. Deliverables: 

- Attached pack (redwood-dpf-evidence-mapping.xlsx) — sheet 1 is control mapping, sheet 2 is subprocessor roster with DPA/SCC status, sheet 3 is log samples (redacted).
- network-topology-plain.pdf — shows EU-primary routing and documented fallback paths (we pin EU-tagged workloads to EU regions; cache replicas are TTL-limited and encrypted).
- sccs-signed-template.pdf — the template we use; we can provide executed copies for named subprocessors on request.

Short clarifications (answers to your bullets):
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 for all service endpoints; AES-256-GCM at rest. Service keys managed by Redwood KMS (AWS KMS in hosted deployments) with 90-day rotation. For Dedicated/Private, we support customer-managed keys (BYOK).
- Subprocessors: Current roster attached. Three recent infra vendors are contract-complete; confirmed by Laura (cc'd) — executed DPAs with SCCs where applicable.
- Network routing: EU-tagged ingestion and inference stay in EU by default; we included the fallback logic where automated regional failover could route to a nearby region for latency resiliency (this is logged and customers can opt-out).
- Supplementary measures: Customer key separation, strict egress ACLs, monthly patching cadence for inference infra, and continuous integration tests for config drift enforcement.
- Logs/audit: Default request trace retention 90 days; extended retention under Dedicated/Private. Redacted examples included in workbook. We can produce a longer audit package under NDA.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm if the workbook format is sufficient for Helix's DPF committee.
2) If executed SCCs for specific subprocessors are required, let us know which ones and we'll queue requests (typical SLA: 3–7 business days to retrieve executed contracts).
3) If Helix wants an on-call walkthrough, we can schedule a 45-minute technical session this week — propose Wed/Thu mornings CET.

Thanks — happy to dig deeper on any point.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference
